name: Source-Scaling Indicator Laws
statement: In a fixed union-closed orientation, $\varepsilon_0=0$ exactly when every ambient normalized row array has a feasible sufficiently small common-scaling tail, and $\varepsilon_\infty=0$ exactly when every ambient normalized row array has a feasible sufficiently large tail; in either case the existence of one such tail suffices and $\mathcal A(C)\cong\mathbb R^{d_C}$. The reflected minima $\eta_b$ are nonincreasing under nonempty pc-minors and satisfy $\eta_b(C\times D)=\max\{\eta_b(C),\eta_b(D)\}$ for $b\in\{0,\infty\}$.
proof: Empty retained positive systems work for every array, while a uniformly small ratio array obstructs every nonempty retained system. Acyclic negative systems admit witnesses by reverse topological order, while a directed cycle is obstructed by ratios larger than one. Specified-minor coefficient maps commute with common scaling, and source systems of a product are disjoint unions of the factor systems.
